chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Aslam, from Al-Khattab ibn Mus'ab, from Sadeer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
A man does not leave assisting his Muslim brother until he strives in it and consoles him, except that he will be tried with assisting one who sins and he will not be recompensed.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of neglecting to actively assist a Muslim brother?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) warns that passive neglect of a brother's need results in a specific spiritual trial: being burdened with assisting a sinful person who yields no reward. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on 'active' charity (not just giving, but striving and consoling), linking social responsibility directly to one's own spiritual state. The consequence serves as a divine mechanism to ensure that those who ignore righteous needs are compensated by aiding the less deserving, highlighting the balance of justice in social interactions.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Hassan, from Muhammad Bin Aslam, from Al Khattab Bin Mus’ab, from Sadeyr, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A man would not leave assisting his Muslim brother until he strives regarding it and consoling him except that he would be Tried with assisting one who sins and he would not be Recompensed (for assisting him)’.
en.sarwar: 3. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from Muhammad ibn Hassan from Muhammad ibn Aslam from al-Khattab ibn Mas’ab ibn Sadir from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“Whoever ignores assistance to his Muslim brother and the endeavor to cooperate with him will be involved in assisting someone who commits sins. It (assistance) does not bring him any rewards.”
